raw_case_text:
A 59-year-old male patient was admitted to our university hospital (Botucatu, SP, Brazil) complaining of a perianal suppurative ulcer developed two months before the first medical consultation. He was under therapy with prednisone 40 mg/day for six months due to a presumed diagnosis of a drug reaction. On physical examination, a clean 10-cm diameter phagedenic perianal ulcer (Figure 1) and two longitudinal suppurative ulcers on the inguino-crural region were observed. During investigation, and soon after reducing the corticosteroid dose, disseminated erythematous papules and nodules were observed in the upper limbs (Figure 2).Histopathology of the perianal ulcer revealed a dense histiocytic dermal infiltrate and a granulomatous inflammatory response with central caseous necrosis (Figure 3). Fite-Faraco staining showed a few acid-fast bacilli and the hypothesis of cutaneous tuberculosis was raised. The histopathology of upper limbs papular and nodular lesions showed foamy macrophages with globi of bacilli, suggesting lepromatous leprosy (Figure 4). The perianal and inguinal ulcers were considered uncommon manifestations of type 2 leprosy developed when corticosteroid was gradually diminished. The patient was treated as for multibacillary leprosy with multidrug therapy and thalidomide.
Four weeks later, the patient had fever, weight loss, asthenia and worsening of the perianal ulcer (Figure 5), but without erythema nodosum leprosum. With this clinical picture, new investigation was developed. The tuberculin skin test was positive (20 x 20 mm) and culture of M. tuberculosis - using a biopsy sample from the perianal ulcer - on Lowenstein-Jensen medium was positive (Figure 6). Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and DNA analysis from upper limb skin samples were positive for M. leprae (Figure 7). With the new information the patient was finally diagnosed as presenting simultaneously lepromatous leprosy - type 2 reaction - and cutaneous tuberculosis expressed by the perianal ulcer. Screening for HIV, HBV or HCV infection as well as lung, renal or colon compromising were negative. Hence, the patient was treated with isoniazid, ethambutol and rifampin for nine months with complete healing of the perianal and inguinal lesions after two months (Figure 8). After the tuberculosis treatment, the patient was submitted to additional multidrug therapy for 12 months with dapsone, rifampin and clofazimine with complete cure of leprosy.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 59-year-old male in Botucatu, Brazil, presented with a 2-month history of a large suppurative perianal ulcer and bilateral inguinocrural ulcers.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed a progressive suppurative perianal ulcer 2 months prior to admission while taking oral prednisone 40 mg/day for 6 months for a presumed drug reaction. Shortly after inpatient corticosteroid tapering was initiated, he developed disseminated erythematous papules and nodules over his upper extremities; 4 weeks after starting leprosy therapy and thalidomide, he experienced fever, weight loss, asthenia, and worsening of the perianal ulcer without erythema nodosum leprosum.
subjective.past_medical_history: Six-month history of oral prednisone (40 mg/day) for a presumed drug eruption.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for perianal and inguinal ulceration, subsequent upper limb eruption, fever, weight loss, and asthenia.

objective.physical_examination: Initial physical examination revealed a clean 10-cm phagedenic perianal ulcer and two longitudinal suppurative ulcers in the inguinocrural folds; following corticosteroid dose reduction, disseminated erythematous papules and nodules appeared on both upper limbs.
objective.routine_investigations: Serological screening for HIV, HBV, and HCV as well as pulmonary, renal, and colonic evaluations were negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Biopsy of the perianal ulcer showed a dense histiocytic dermal infiltrate and granulomatous inflammation with central caseous necrosis and sparse acid-fast bacilli on Fite-Faraco staining, while biopsy of the upper limb papulonodular lesions demonstrated foamy macrophages containing globi of AFB. At 4-week reassessment, tuberculin skin test (TST) was strongly reactive (20 x 20 mm), and Lowenstein-Jensen culture of the perianal ulcer biopsy and PCR/DNA analysis of the upper limb skin biopsy were performed.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Lowenstein-Jensen culture of the perianal ulcer isolated Mycobacterium tuberculosis while PCR and DNA analysis of the upper limb nodules confirmed Mycobacterium leprae, establishing a final diagnosis of concurrent multibacillary lepromatous leprosy (with Type 2 reaction) and perianal/inguinal cutaneous tuberculosis (orificial/scrofuloderma-type tuberculosis, initially misinterpreted as a necrotic Type 2 lepra reaction). Following initial multibacillary MDT and thalidomide, the patient completed a 9-month anti-tubercular regimen (isoniazid, ethambutol, and rifampin) with complete healing of the perianal and inguinal ulcers within 2 months, followed by an additional 12 months of multibacillary MDT (dapsone, rifampin, and clofazimine) achieving complete cure of leprosy.
